purpose: Bounded California route from Los Angeles wildfire and smoke exposure through insurance claim processing, regulator enforcement, repair standards, and open safe-return recovery.

events.geography: Los Angeles County Eaton and Palisades wildfire claims; California Department of Insurance statewide regulatory response
events.date_precision: Claims tracker updated July 6, 2026; State Farm investigation announced May 4, 2026; smoke-restoration legislation signed September 15, 2026
events.denominator: California Department of Insurance tracker totals for filed and partially paid claims, not unique households or property-level completion; State Farm review sampled 220 claims
events.method: Official California Department of Insurance claims tracker, enforcement announcement, and enacted smoke-damage recovery standards; aggregate and sampled regulatory units are not pooled
events.missingness: Unique household identity, property-level payment amount, claim timing, living-expense adequacy, repair completion, safe return, renewal, move/stay decision, health, trust, and later security are not linked in the retained record
events.exposure: Eaton and Palisades wildfire and smoke damage generated 41,727 reported claims; 40,482 were reported partially paid and $25.2 billion was reported paid to date
events.alternatives_before_action: Temporary lodging, living-expense coverage, borrowing, family support, public aid, repair, sale, or moving may be alternatives, but the aggregate tracker does not show which were available, affordable, or used by each household
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Insurance claims and partial payments provide a formal recovery route while leaving repairability, smoke testing, communication, and safe occupancy unresolved; sampled claims included delayed investigation, underpayment, and smoke-damage disputes
events.choice_or_response: California reviewed a sample of 220 State Farm claims and identified 398 violations in 114 claims; the Department also reported aggregate recovery from insurers and urged formal assistance for delay or denial complaints
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Insurers and adjusters control investigation, valuation, payment, and communication; the Department controls regulatory oversight; households control some complaint, repair, stay, and move decisions but their resources are not retained
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Regulator enforcement and a September 2026 law created enforceable standards for investigating, testing, and restoring smoke-damaged homes; implementation at a particular property is not observed
events.immediate_outcome: The official record establishes a claim and partial-payment stage plus regulatory correction while keeping household repairability and stable housing open
events.protected_outcome: Safe repair, habitable housing, financial continuity, and the ability to remain could be protected by adequate payment and enforceable restoration, but no property-level protected outcome is verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Housing stability, money, time, health, work, neighborhood attachment, and future insurability may be sacrificed; the aggregate record does not identify the household trade-off
events.cost_risk_transfer: Claim handling can transfer rebuilding, smoke-testing, living-expense, and uncertainty costs between insurers, households, contractors, lenders, and public agencies; the public record does not quantify that transfer
events.later_outcome: No same-property final payment, repair completion, safe return, renewal, stable stay, move, health, or later household security is observed
events.meaning_and_attribution: A household may interpret partial payment or enforcement as protection, delay, unfairness, or proof that remaining in place is too risky; blame, trust, and attribution are not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: Department enforcement, complaint assistance, and enacted smoke-restoration standards are observed; household organizing, political action, insurer switching, and later public response are not linked
events.counterexample: Partial payment is not necessarily inadequate, and a sampled violation cannot be generalized to every insurer or claim; aggregate paid dollars cannot establish a household recovery rate
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official California Department of Insurance aggregate tracker and regulatory records; claim counts, paid totals, sampled violations, and legislation are different units and do not establish property-level adequacy or causation

arrows.evidence: California reports 41,727 claims filed, 40,482 partially paid, and $25.2 billion paid to date for the Eaton and Palisades wildfire claims tracker
arrows.counterexample: The counts are not unique households, and partial payment does not establish full payment, adequacy, repair, or safe return
arrows.remaining_gap: Property-level claim, payment amount, living-expense route, repair cost, and household timing

arrows.evidence: California reviewed 220 State Farm claims and identified 398 violations in 114 claims, including delayed investigation, underpayment, adjuster changes, smoke-damage disputes, and poor communication
arrows.counterexample: The sample is an enforcement review, not a statewide violation rate or evidence that every claim had the same experience
arrows.remaining_gap: Claim-level correction, payment timing, property repair, and household confirmation

arrows.evidence: California signed AB 1795 on September 15, 2026, establishing enforceable standards for investigating, testing, and restoring smoke-damaged homes
arrows.counterexample: A legal standard does not establish implementation, contractor availability, payment, or a completed safe repair at any specific property
arrows.remaining_gap: Property implementation, compliance, testing, restoration, occupancy, and recurrence

arrows.to: repair completion, safe return, and stable housing
arrows.evidence: The tracker and regulatory records do not link a unique property to final payment, completed repair, safe occupancy, renewal, or a stay/move outcome
arrows.counterexample: A household may repair and remain safely, move voluntarily, or use public/lender support without that outcome appearing in the claims aggregate
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-property final payment, repair, occupancy, renewal, move/stay, health, and household security

arrows.to: trust, insurer switching, complaint, or political action
arrows.evidence: California provides complaint assistance and regulatory response, but no affected-household trust, switching, organizing, or later action is linked
arrows.counterexample: A household may remain with an insurer because of dependence or lack of alternatives rather than trust; a complaint is not proof of later political action
arrows.remaining_gap: Direct household interpretation, complaint resolution, renewal/switching, trust, and action

boundary: This ledger formalizes an aggregate California wildfire-claims, sampled enforcement, and smoke-restoration standards route. It does not establish property-level payment adequacy, repair completion, safe return, insurer causation, household displacement, trust, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only official California Department of Insurance aggregate claims, sampled enforcement, enacted standards, and interpretation limits are retained; policyholder files, adjuster records, and property-level claim data are not stored.
